previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a recent history of aortic valve replacement and coronary artery bypass grafting presented with brief episodes of palpitations and left-sided chest pain. She had been recovering at home but developed symptoms accompanied by a non-productive cough. Evaluation revealed stable vital signs, no significant pericardial effusion, and EKG changes attributed to left ventricular hypertrophy rather than acute ischemia. A chest X-ray showed new left lower lobe collapse, likely contributing to her discomfort. She remained in normal sinus rhythm, tolerated hemodialysis without issue, and responded well to pain management and respiratory support. Her medications were adjusted, including restarting isosorbide mononitrate at a lower dose and increasing metoprolol. With symptom resolution and stable condition, she was discharged home on the second day with instructions for wound care, activity restrictions, and follow-up appointments.

Active Issues:
# Hypotension: Pt reports lightheadedness upon standing and low 
BP on her home monitor after taking her home meds.  Husband 
reports patient having near syncopal episode on her way to 
bedroom.  Thought to be orthostatic hypotension ___ significant 
fluid removal from HD earlier in the week.  Patient does report 
fever to tmax 101.2 at ___ prior to this admission 
though this is not documented in the outside records received 
here and patient remained afebrile throughout admission.  Blood 
cultures at ___ and here were negative to date.  
Orthostatics were additionally negative though patient reported 
feeling dizzy.  She was bolused 250cc NS on ___ and then 
walked the halls without any difficulty.  Her dizziness 
improved.  Her Clonidine was downtitrated to 0.1mg BID daily as 
opposed to 0.2 mg BID.  She was never truly hypotensive here, 
though for this patient her BPs at 130-157/55-57 with occasional 
SBP between 115-120 represent relative hypotension for her. If 
her blood pressure remains low as an outpatient, recommendation 
would be to downtitrate or even take patient off of Carvedilol 
in favor of more beta specific anti hypertensive (if needed). 
We, however, expect that her BP will increase again once the 
hypovolemia resolves. In that case, we will continmue to aim for 
target BP of <140/90 mmHe and may decide to add Clonidine 0.1 mg 
as needed to achieve that goal.
